items.title: Semrush Unveils New Brand Identity to Lead in AI Search Era
items.summary: Semrush has overhauled its brand to become a unified intelligence engine amid a 527% YoY surge in AI-driven search. The platform leverages 27B keywords and 43T backlinks to help brands win visibility in AI agents like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews. This positions Semrush at the forefront of SEO-AI convergence as traditional search evolves.

items.title: Over The Top SEO Launches First Full-Scale GEO Division
items.summary: Over The Top SEO has deployed a dedicated Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) division with over 450 optimized pages already indexed. Targeting AI answers in ChatGPT (60% market share) and Google AI Overviews, this marks the first major agency operationalizing GEO amid the shift from page rankings to AI citations. GEO focuses on being named directly in generative responses.

items.title: 3 AI Search Changes Every Marketer Needs a Plan For in Q2
items.summary: Search Engine Journal highlights three pivotal AI search developments requiring immediate marketer strategies, including adaptations to Google AI integrations and evolving SERPs. As AI overviews expand, content must prioritize E-E-A-T and structured data for visibility. This comes amid ongoing volatility from unannounced Google core updates.

items.title: Open-Source GEO-SEO Claude Tool Trends for AI Visibility Audits
items.summary: SEO communities on X are raving about the new open-source 'geo-seo-claude' tool that runs comprehensive GEO audits using parallel AI agents. It scores sites for AI citation readiness across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and Google AIO, checking crawlers, schema, E-E-A-T, and generating reports. With AI traffic up 527% YoY, it's a free game-changer for adapting to generative search.

items.title: HubSpot: AI Reshaping SEO with AEO, GEO, and Zero-Click Searches
items.summary: HubSpot's guide on AI's SEO impact is circulating on X, detailing how chatbots and Google AI Overviews drive zero-click results and reduce top-funnel traffic. Marketers must adapt via Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), stronger E-E-A-T signals, structured content, and technical optimizations. This reflects the rapid evolution in search behavior.

items.title: New SEO Frontier: AEO, GEO, SXO, ACO Empower Small Brands in AI Era
items.summary: X discussion highlights the shift from traditional SEO (backlinks, DA) to 'New SEO' focusing on AI citations in LLMs like ChatGPT and Perplexity, enabling small brands to compete with giants. Key tactics include AEO, GEO, Search Experience Optimization (SXO), and Agentic Commerce Optimization (ACO) via structured data and topical authority. Tools like Pierview.ai track AI mentions as new KPIs.

items.title: Grammarly Introduces AI Agents Modeled After Real Authors Without Permission
items.summary: Grammarly, once a basic proofreading tool, now features AI 'expert' agents based on real authors, including some deceased, without seeking permission. The post raises concerns about the ethical implications of using authors' styles for AI-generated feedback. This development highlights blurring lines between human and machine contributions in writing assistance.

items.title: Scarlett Press Acquires Two Books from Georgia Bowers in Six-Figure Pre-Empt Deal
items.summary: Scarlett Press, an imprint of Simon & Schuster UK, has secured a six-figure pre-empt deal for two books by author Georgia Bowers. The announcement underscores significant investment in new literary works. Details shared via The Bookseller on X.

items.title: BookTok's Influence Reshaping Publishing: From Prose Rejection to Algorithm-Driven Releases
items.summary: Recent headlines highlight BookTok rejecting third-person prose, prompting publisher panic, and algorithms now determining what gets published. With 59 million romance readers, publishers are incorporating BookTok elements directly into book covers. The post positions BookTok as TikTok's literary community driving industry changes.

items.title: Writer Sues Grammarly for Creating Unauthorized AI Editors from Authors' Works
items.summary: A writer has filed a lawsuit against Grammarly for transforming her and other authors into AI 'editors' without consent. The company allegedly uses authors' data to generate feedback mimicking their styles. This legal action addresses growing concerns over AI training on creators' content.

items.title: Publishers Including Big Five Sue Shadow Library Allegedly Fueling AI Chatbots
items.summary: A coalition of major publishers, including Hachette, Penguin Random House, HarperCollins, Macmillan, and Simon & Schuster, is suing a shadow library. The site is accused of providing pirated books to power AI chatbots. The litigation seeks to curb unauthorized use of copyrighted materials in AI development.

items.title: UK Society of Authors Launches Logo to Certify Human-Written Books Amid AI Rise
items.summary: The UK Society of Authors has introduced a logo and registration scheme to identify books written by humans, not AI. Announced by Tracy Chevalier at the London Book Fair, it responds to increasing AI-generated content in publishing. Thousands of authors have also published an empty book protesting AI theft of their works.

items.title: 'The Bride!' Feminist Remake Bombs at Box Office Amid Woke Messaging Complaints
items.summary: Maggie Gyllenhaal's 'The Bride!', a feminist reimagining of the Bride of Frankenstein starring Christian Bale, opened to just $7.3 million domestically, far below expectations for its $90 million budget. The film was crushed by Pixar's 'Hoppers' at $46 million and even 'Scream 7's second weekend. Audience backlash highlighted heavy-handed themes of male oppression, consent, and MeToo, resulting in a C+ CinemaScore and poor word-of-mouth.

items.title: Rachel Zegler Calls 'Snow White' Casting Backlash 'Really Confusing'
items.summary: Rachel Zegler discussed the intense backlash to her role in Disney's live-action Snow White remake, which suffered a $170 million loss partly due to audience rejection of changes to the story. She described the criticism as confusing in a recent Harper's Bazaar interview. The controversy continues to fuel debates on remakes and representation.

items.title: Pixar Chief Explains Cutting LGBTQ Storyline from 'Elio': 'Not Hundreds of Millions of Therapy'
items.summary: Pete Docter, Pixar's chief creative officer, revealed the studio removed an LGBTQ storyline from the upcoming 'Elio' to focus on storytelling rather than therapy. The decision comes amid industry scrutiny over preachy content in films. It reflects broader shifts following recent flops attributed to ideological elements.

items.title: Viral Post Lists 'Red Flags' for Woke TV and Movies That Prompt Instant Turn-Offs
items.summary: Byl Holte shared a popular thread detailing tropes like black characters in medieval settings, strong female bosses, pronoun declarations, and climate lectures that signal 'wokeness,' causing him to stop watching. The post resonated widely, amassing over 12,000 likes and sparking discussions on audience avoidance of such content. It highlights common viewer frustrations with ideological insertions over entertainment.

items.title: Variety Reports 'The Bride!' Collapses with $7.3M Opening as 'Hoppers' Dominates
items.summary: Variety's post on Maggie Gyllenhaal’s feminist 'The Bride!' notes its box office flop at $7.3 million opening weekend. Pixar's 'Hoppers' scored massively higher, underscoring contrasting receptions. Comments tied the underperformance to perceptions of overemphasis on messaging.

items.title: Hollywood's Woke Mind Virus Blamed for Industry Collapse and Flops Like Snow White
items.summary: A detailed post analyzes entertainment's shift to propaganda over profit, citing Disney's Snow White $170M loss due to woke remakes and audience withdrawal. It points to the 'woke mind virus' infecting motives and calls for a reset to entertainment focus. References recent box office duds and studio retreats from DEI.

items.title: Small Businesses Are the Biggest Untapped AI Opportunity
items.summary: Nozz (@NoahEpstein_) reveals how automating simple tasks like appointment reminders for a PE firm's hairdresser led to $200k in work, shifting his view on the industry. He argues small businesses represent massive AI potential overlooked amid hype for bigger niches. The post includes a full breakdown and playbook for landing SMB clients through top-down adoption via owners or investors.

items.title: What Small Business Owners Are Quietly Building with AI
items.summary: Wonder Of Things shares real-world examples of non-coders using AI effectively: a dentist's AI receptionist saving $4k/month, food truck demand predictor cutting waste 40%, photographer's AI editor doubling bookings, gym churn predictor upping retention 22%, and pest control custom CRM replacing $1.2k/month software. These tools deliver tangible results in operations, customer service, and efficiency. The post warns that builders will outpace those just 'staying informed,' widening survival gaps.

items.title: ECI Releases AI Readiness Report as SMB AI Optimism Outpaces Adoption
items.summary: ECI's report shows SMB leaders in manufacturing, distribution, and field services are bullish on AI to tackle labor shortages and ops challenges, with over 70% positive views. However, gaps in data readiness, expertise, and starting points mean nearly 40% see no measurable results, despite demand for data analysis (60%) and marketing (49%). It offers guidance on integrable AI solutions to boost adoption.

items.title: AI Agents Take Aim At The Local Marketing Agency As Mega Raises $11.5 Million
items.summary: Mega, a Brooklyn-based platform, deploys AI agents to automate marketing for small businesses ($500k-$20M revenue) like dentists and contractors, handling search optimization, ads, and websites via a simple dashboard. It disrupts local agencies by enabling continuous optimization without dedicated teams. The company secured $11.5M Series A from Goodwater, a16z, and others to expand into email and social.
